persona.who: 22, wants to be a filmmaker, father is a government doctor who wants him to do MBBS or at least MBA. Fights every dinner.
persona.note: papa says films are for rich kids and I should do MBA. we fight every night. I love him and I also feel like he doesn't see me at all. mummy cries in the kitchen

understanding.emotion: torn between love and being unseen
understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call being seen as less than you are, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.core_struggle: A student under twenty-five is being told by their father to abandon films for an MBA, and feels their father does not see them at all, while their mother cries.
understanding.mirror: You love the man who fights with you every night, and you carry your mother's tears.
understanding.insight: It isn't the films he's fighting. It's the person he cannot see behind them. And your mother's tears are not your fault, but they are your burden.
understanding.mechanism_label: Being seen as less than you are

queries.hook: Being seen as less than you are by the person you love most, and the ache of watching your mother cry while the fight plays out again.
queries.diagnose: When a parent sees only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what he sees; your worth was never his to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing to him gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and find the courage the moment asks for without breaking the love.
queries.story: A young seeker whose elders dismissed their path, who stood in their truth and found their footing without turning away from the ones they loved.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
verse.sanskrit: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते । क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप ॥
verse.line: This smallness of heart isn't who you are. Shake it off and stand up.
verse.translation: Do not give in to this unmanliness, Partha; it does not become you. Throw off this petty weakness of heart and rise, scorcher of enemies.
verse.why: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.
verse.misuse: Not 'feelings are weakness' or 'man up'. It is a friend reminding you of your strength, said once, then explained for 700 verses.

prasang.title: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasang.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
prasang.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

verse.meaning: Krishna sees Arjuna on the battlefield, crying and ready to drop his bow. He tells Arjuna not to give in to this unmanliness. It does not suit who you are. Throw off this petty weakness of heart and rise. This is a friend reminding you of your strength, not telling you that feelings are a flaw. Admitting you are lost and asking for help is where clarity begins.
verse.for_you: Your father sees a film student and a problem. He does not see the person who is still learning who they are. You do not have to shrink to fit his view of you. Your path is your own, even if it feels messy right now.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
verse.line: Better your own path done imperfectly than someone else's done perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, even done imperfectly, than the duty of another well done. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is full of fear.
verse.why: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.
verse.misuse: Not 'stay in the role your family or birth assigned you'. It's about being true to your own nature and calling.

prasang.title: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasang.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.
prasang.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna, who is paralyzed by doubt and fear of failure. Arjuna has been told by their elders and peers to follow a path that is not theirs, and Krishna is pointing out that following someone else's script is full of fear. Borrowed lives are dangerous. The verse proposes that your own path, even if it looks messy or imperfect from the outside, is safer and truer than a borrowed one. It asks you to stop measuring yourself against a standard that was never yours to meet.
verse.for_you: Think about the way your father sees the films you love. He sees a rich kid's hobby. You see your life. The path he wants for you is borrowed. It is done perfectly in his head, but it is not yours.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verse.sanskrit: त्वया व्याप्तमिदं विश्वं त्वयि प्रोतं यथार्थतः । शुद्धबुद्धस्वरूपस्त्वं मा गमः क्षुद्रचित्तताम् ॥
verse.line: You are pure awareness, wider than any worry. Don't let your mind shrink into pettiness.
verse.translation: This whole universe is pervaded by you and strung on you. By nature you are pure awareness; do not fall into smallness of mind.
verse.why: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

prasang.title: Janaka asks the boy-sage how to be free
prasang.summary: King Janaka, ruler of Mithila, asks the young sage Ashtavakra three questions: how to gain wisdom, freedom and dispassion. Ashtavakra answers at once: you are not the body or your roles but the awareness that watches them, and freedom is available now.
prasang.story_hook: A powerful king bowed before a boy whose body was bent in eight places, and asked him how to be free.
prasang.lesson: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

verse.meaning: The young sage Ashtavakra is speaking to King Janaka, who is asking how to find freedom while still living in the world. Ashtavakra tells him that the whole universe is strung on him, and by nature he is pure awareness. He warns him not to fall into smallness of mind. The verse proposes that you are the space in which all your roles and worries happen, not the roles themselves. Freedom begins when you stop letting your mind shrink into the pettiness of being judged.
verse.for_you: When you are in the kitchen and hear your mother cry, or when your father says films are for rich kids, your mind shrinks. You shrink. But you are the awareness that sees all of it. You are wider than his words and her tears. Do not fall into that smallness.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She tells him to stop holding himself in contempt and to stop settling for so little. She says to set his mind on what is truly good and to pull himself together. The truth underneath is that past failure does not define you, and those who never try never succeed.
verse.for_you: Your father cannot see the person who wants to study films. You do not have to shrink into what he expects of you. Hold on to the truth that your worth is not a debate.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verse.sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Speak words that don't wound, that are true, kind and helpful. That is discipline of speech.
verse.translation: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of sacred texts: this is called austerity of speech.
verse.why: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.
verse.misuse: Kind speech doesn't mean avoiding hard truths; it means saying them without cruelty.

prasang.title: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that speech should not wound, and should be true, pleasant and helpful. This is the discipline of speech. The truth is that kind speech does not mean avoiding hard truths, it means saying them without cruelty. It should also be given without strings.
verse.for_you: When you speak with your father tonight, you can say what you need without cruelty. You can tell him you are choosing films, and you can do it with a steady voice.

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram is struck by how Hanuman, a stranger and envoy, has just spoken to them.
verse.sanskrit: अविस्तरमसंदिग्धमविलम्बितमव्यथम्। उरःस्थं कण्ठगं वाक्यं वर्तते मध्यमस्वरम्॥
verse.line: Not too long, not vague, not rushed, not strained, in an even voice: that is how to speak.
verse.translation: His words were not long-winded, not ambiguous, not rushed, not strained; they came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone.
verse.why: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

prasang.title: Sugriva's fear and Hanuman's first words
prasang.summary: The exiled Sugriva sees two armed strangers and panics, sure his brother has sent assassins. Hanuman calms him and goes in disguise to find out. His speech to the brothers is so clear and gentle that Ram is moved and trusts him at once.
prasang.story_hook: Sugriva saw two archers walking towards his hill and was sure they had come to kill him.
prasang.lesson: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

verse.meaning: Ram tells Lakshman that Hanuman spoke to them with words that were not long-winded, not vague, not rushed, not strained. They came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone. The truth is that fear jumps ahead of facts, and calm, clear words build trust fast.
verse.for_you: When you tell your father about films tomorrow, you can speak with a calm, even voice. You do not have to rush or strain. You can just say the truth clearly, and let him hear it.

story.title: Sutikshna runs to meet Ram
story.story_hook: A young sage ran out of his hut to meet Ram and, halfway there, forgot which way he was going.
story.summary: A young sage hears Ram is near and runs out, sure he has no devotion, wisdom or discipline worth anything, trusting only that Ram loves those with nowhere else to go. Lost in love he wanders, dances, forgets the way; Ram watches from behind a tree, then lifts him up and holds him. Asked for a boon, the sage says only: may this one pride never leave me, that I am his.
story.lesson: You don't have to feel qualified; the one with nowhere else to go is the one he loves.

anchor.speaker: Sutikshna
anchor.setting: The young sage Sutikshna hears Ram is coming and runs to meet him, full of doubt about himself.
anchor.sanskrit: सहित अनुज मोहि राम गोसाईं। मिलिहहिं निज सेवक की नाईं॥ मोरे जियँ भरोस दृढ़ नाहीं। भगति बिरति न ग्यान मन माहीं ॥ नहिं सतसंग जोग जप जागा। नहिं दृढ़ चरन कमल अनुरागा॥ एक बानि करुनानिधान की। सो प्रिय जाकें गति न आन की ॥
anchor.line: I have no devotion, no wisdom, no steady love. But he loves the one who has nowhere else to go.
anchor.translation: 'Will Ram, my master, with his brother, meet me as he would his own servant? There is no firm trust in my heart; no devotion, detachment or wisdom in my mind; no good company, no yoga, chanting or sacrifice, no steady love for his lotus feet. But the ocean of compassion has one habit: the one who has no other refuge is dear to him.'
anchor.why: You don't have to feel qualified; the one with nowhere else to go is the one he loves.
anchor.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.

weeks.title: Unseen by the one you love

script: You are caught between your father's plans and the person you are trying to become. You spend hours on your phone, and every night brings another fight. You feel unseen by the one person who should know you best.

Arjuna stands on the battlefield, his bow slack in his hands. He is weeping, refusing to lift his weapons against his own people. Krishna watches him, not with anger, but with a steady concern. He sees his friend collapsing under a grief he cannot yet name. And Krishna replies:
क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते, क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप.
In plain words: This smallness of heart isn't who you are. Shake it off and stand up.

Krishna is not calling Arjuna weak. He is calling him back to himself. This smallness is a moment, not a life. It is the despair that comes when you cannot see the path forward. Admitting you are lost is not defeat. It is the only place where clarity can actually begin. You do not have to carry the weight of your father's disappointment alone.

Your father sees a film student and a problem. He does not see the person who is still learning who they are. You do not have to shrink to fit his view of you. Your path is your own, even if it feels messy right now.
What would it look like to stand up, just a little bit, today?

depth.practice: Write down the exact words your father used to describe your future. Put them on a piece of paper. Read them once. Then take a deep breath and let the paper go.
depth.question: What part of you feels like it is still becoming?
